lessons.taskOriginal:
Return the names of all border summits (lying in more than one country) with prominence over 300 m, most prominent first. Also output the prominence and the number of countries. Columns: ?name, ?prominence, ?countryCount. Prominence is stored as a string. Catch: for Dufourspitze the country is a single value "Switzerland and Italy".
Data: four-thousanders.ttl (82 summits). Prefixes: uiaa-s: <https://www.theuiaa.org/4000-alps/schema/>, uiaa: <https://www.theuiaa.org/4000-alps/summit/>. Ranges (uiaa-s:inRange) are bare IRIs with no names; output the IRI itself.

Open the schema (the editor already holds four-thousanders-schema.ttl) and extend it. a) A class route with the properties route name and difficulty grade, plus a property linking a summit to its normal route. Document every new class and property with SKOS like the rest: skos:inScheme, skos:prefLabel, skos:definition, rdfs:domain, rdfs:range. b) A separate SKOS concept scheme with the grades F, PD, AD, D, TD, ED: each with a skos:notation and a French prefLabel (facile, peu difficile, assez difficile, difficile, très difficile, extrêmement difficile). PD- and PD+ are narrower (skos:narrower) than PD. The difficulty-grade property from a) points to these concepts (domain: route).
Choose the IRI names yourself (the uiaa-s: prefix is already declared).
